subject: Audit playbook & evidence routing — clarifying intake and regional exceptions
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit playbook & evidence routing — clarifying intake and regional exceptions

Hi team,

I pulled together an initial draft of the auditor playbook for the upcoming Acme Health ISO/FedRAMP intake (attached as playbook-draft.md) and an updated evidence index (attached). Before we lock anything down for the auditor kickoff next week I need to resolve a few routing and sampling questions that will change how we package evidence and who owns requests across regions. High-level asks below — please reply with owners and ETA (this week if possible):

1) Regional evidence routing: Acme has environments in US and EU. We need a clear rule for evidence that contains EU personal data (logs, user exports). Do we: (a) host the evidence snapshot in the EU drive and provide a presigned link, or (b) produce redacted artifacts and ship to US auditors?

2) Data residency + auditor access window: For FedRAMP scoping we may be asked for live access to staging for a 48-hour observation window. Operationally, is Security comfortable granting time-limited read-only access to CertifyCo? If not, what is the fallback (recorded session + logs export)?

3) Sampling methodology: Simon will request SOC 2 control samples for a rolling 90-day window. Do we default to contiguous time-based slices (e.g., consecutive 30-day windows) or representative event-based samples? The playbook currently recommends time-based but I want buy-in from Ops.

4) Evidence formats & chain of custody: Some auditors insist on raw logs + MD5 hashes; others accept aggregated CSVs and screenshots. Confirm our baseline deliverable per evidence type (config changes, logs, backups, KMS rotation records).

5) KMS/HSM: If an auditor asks for KMS key-rotation proofs, are we comfortable providing KMS audit logs + key UUIDs, or do we need an HSM vendor letter?

6) Scheduling conflict escalation: auditors requested a week that collides with an internal deploy blackout. Who can sign an exception if we must extend the blackout?

Attachments: playbook-draft.md, evidence_index_v2.xlsx

Proposed owners:
- Regional routing: Marissa
- Sampling methodology: Vivek
- KMS/HSM + chain of custody: Olga

Please mark any items you can't own and suggest alternatives. I will update the playbook in Drive (link below) and then send to Simon with the clarified plan.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@certifyco.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Audit playbook & evidence routing — clarifying intake and regional exceptions

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the draft — looks good. Quick clarifications from the auditor side so we can finalize the request set:

- For EU-resident logs: our preference is to receive a standalone archive (SFTP or presigned link) that stays in-region. Redaction adds risk to sampling. If you can provide a region-scoped archive with hashes, that's ideal.

- Access window: a 48-hour read-only observation is normal, but we only need API/log access for specific endpoints and time ranges. A recorded session can work for some controls but not for live key-material access.

- Sampling: we'll accept time-based contiguous slices for system logs, but for user-facing controls we may request event-driven samples (e.g., password resets tied to specific incidents). We'll call out the exact sample IDs in the intake.

- KMS: KMS audit logs with key UUIDs + rotation timestamps are sufficient for most evidence. HSM vendor letters are a plus but not mandatory unless it's required by FedRAMP baselines.

- Preferred formats: CSV/NDJSON exports for logs, signed PDFs for policy docs, and MD5/SHA256 checksums for large archives.

If you can provide the evidence index and indicate what will be in-region vs. global, we can draft the formal evidence request (to minimize back-and-forth).

Cheers,
Simon
Simon Lee
Senior Auditor, CertifyCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@certifyco.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit playbook & evidence routing — clarifying intake and regional exceptions

Hi Simon / Olga,

Thanks Simon — that guidance helps. Quick internal notes and commitments:

- Regional routing: we'll produce region-scoped archives for EU assets and host them on the EU S3 bucket behind a presigned link with a 14-day TTL. Security will provide MD5 and SHA256 checksums for each archive.

- Access window: Ops confirms we can grant a 48-hour read-only view in staging (no write permissions, no key export). For production-level controls that touch key material, we'll provide KMS audit logs and a recorded session; live key access will not be provided.

- Sampling: Vivek will own mapping of control IDs to sample windows. My proposal: default to contiguous 30-day windows for infra/system logs; for user control samples we'll accept event-based IDs when requested by the auditor.

- KMS/HSM: We will provide KMS audit logs + rotation timestamps + key UUIDs. If FedRAMP asks for additional HSM attestation, we'll coordinate with the vendor and provide an attestation letter.

Action items:
- Vivek: create the control->sample mapping by EOD Thu 12 Aug (Vivek: will you take this?).
- Olga: finalize chain-of-custody template and add to playbook by Thu evening.
- Marissa: prepare EU archived snapshots and checksum manifests for Acme by Fri 13 Aug.

Simon — once we complete the mapping we will send a single, consolidated evidence packet (with checksums and access instructions). Would you prefer a HubSpot ticket listing each artifact or a single zip + manifest?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
